citation.note: Written Notice at Hire: Montana has no required written notice to the employee at hire about at-will status or wage-theft prevention; no state form mandated.
Record Format: No state requirement for paper vs.
Pay frequency: 10-day maximum hold: MCA § 39-3-204 caps wage withholding at 10 business days after wages are earned and due; no frequency mandate (weekly, biweekly, semi-monthly all allowed).
Final pay timing: MCA § 39-3-205 requires immediate payment on involuntary termination unless the employer has a written policy extending to the next payday or 15 days, whichever is sooner.

body.deadline_description: Final pay timing: MCA § 39-3-205 requires immediate payment on involuntary termination unless the employer has a written policy extending to the next payday or 15 days, whichever is sooner. Resignations allow next regular payday or 15 days from separation, whichever is sooner. Special rule: if alleged theft is involved, wages may be withheld if employee consents in writing or employer reports to law enforcement within 7 business days; if no charges within 30 days, wages must be paid in full.

citation.note: Non-compete enforcement (MCA § 28-2-703): Flag any non-compete agreements in the employee file.

body.rule: Non-compete enforcement (MCA § 28-2-703): Flag any non-compete agreements in the employee file. Montana generally voids noncompete agreements for employment; only enforce in narrow goodwill-sale or partnership-dissolution contexts. Do not enforce an employment noncompete without legal review and current case law confirmation. If an employee opposes noncompete enforcement and the employer terminates for the opposition, risk of wrongful-discharge and retaliation claims is high.

citation.note: Minimum wage ties to CPI-U annually: MCA § 39-3-404; as of 2026-01-01, $10.85/hour (adjusted annually by inflation, rounded to nearest $0.05).

citation.note: Deductions and Pay Statements: Montana follows federal FLSA rules; only deductions required by law, court order, or written employee authorization are permitted.
Discrimination and Protected Classes (MCA § 49-2-303): Ensure pay changes and terminations do not violate discrimination statutes.
If the employer has written internal procedures for appealing a discharge (other than those in § 39-2-912), the employee must exhaust them before suing for wrongful discharge.
